# The Ontology

The ontology is a queryable canon of software architecture. It holds every principle with its relations and its repair, every term with its definition, every algorithm with its contract, the reasoning that derives them, the layers they live in and how every tension between them is resolved, and every reference from one record to another is a link.

## Application Concerns

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Actuator Tag

- Kind: [artifact](SCHEMA.md#kind-artifact)
- Category: [Application Concerns](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-application-concerns)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A formal definition of the tag for a file that turns an agent's decision into an effect on the world, filed in an actuators folder.

Example
actuators/motor.actuator.ts

How it is checked

Checked by
the naming gate, which refuses a filename whose last segment before the extension is an undeclared tag or differs from its folder's tag

Population
Every filename whose concern slot holds the tag, and the folder holding each such file

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file carrying the tag is created, moved or renamed, or the declared vocabulary changes

Refusal
The lint run fails a file whose tag is undeclared or disagrees with its folder

Observation
Each filename parsed by position against the declared concern vocabulary

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, and passes a conforming file

Authoritative side
The declared concern vocabulary, which a filename's tag and its folder conform to

Depends on
Not answered

Shape it refuses
Not answered

### Coordinator Tag

- Kind: [artifact](SCHEMA.md#kind-artifact)
- Category: [Application Concerns](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-application-concerns)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A formal definition of the tag for a file that owns a lifecycle and drives the collaborators it depends on, filed in a coordinators folder.

Example
coordinators/upload.coordinator.ts

Distinct from
[Service Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-service-tag): A coordinator owns a lifecycle and drives its collaborators, while a service offers a stateful capability that others call.

Distinct from
[Processor Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-processor-tag): A coordinator drives collaborators through a lifecycle, while a processor applies one operation to each item passing through.

How it is checked

Checked by
the naming gate, which refuses a filename whose last segment before the extension is an undeclared tag or differs from its folder's tag

Population
Every filename whose concern slot holds the tag, and the folder holding each such file

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file carrying the tag is created, moved or renamed, or the declared vocabulary changes

Refusal
The lint run fails a file whose tag is undeclared or disagrees with its folder

Observation
Each filename parsed by position against the declared concern vocabulary

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, and passes a conforming file

Authoritative side
The declared concern vocabulary, which a filename's tag and its folder conform to

Depends on
[Coordinator](LEXICON.md#lexicon-coordinator)

Shape it refuses

## Architecture Review Evolution Governance

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Ad-Hoc Design

- Kind: [anti-pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-anti-pattern)
- Category: [Architecture Review Evolution Governance](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-architecture-review-evolution-governance)
- Layer: [Evolution Principles](SCHEMA.md#layer-evolution-principles)

Details

Definition
Designing by improvisation with no deliberate structure or review, so the architecture accretes inconsistently.

Referenced by
[Design Review](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-design-review)

How it is checked

Checked by
[Design Review](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-design-review)

Population
The term's definition and every architecture edge that names the term

Freshness
A verdict stands until the definition, the term's kind or an edge that names it changes

Refusal
The resolution gate fails an edge that resolves to no term, and a definition that opens as another kind

Observation
The resolution validator's pass over every edge target and every definition opening

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite plants a term no edge names, a dangling dependency and a second check home, and the bundled terms pass

Authoritative side
The term record, which every edge that names the term cites

Depends on
Not answered

Shape it refuses
Not answered

## Behavioral Patterns

## Causality / Ordering / Distributed Time

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

## Codebase / System Architecture Styles

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

## Contracts / Interfaces / Compatibility

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

## Control / Coordination / Centralization

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. ## Coordination Surfaces

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

## Core Modular Design

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. ## Core Vocabulary

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Silent Failure

- Kind: [anti-pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-anti-pattern)
- Category: [Core Vocabulary](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-core-vocabulary)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A failure that occurs without surfacing any error, log, or signal, leaving it undetected.

Referenced by
[Fail Fast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-fast), [Logging](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-logging), [Alerting](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-alerting)

Distinct from
[Log-as-Control-Flow](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-log-as-control-flow): A silent failure leaves no signal at all, while log-as-control-flow leaves a log line and carries on as if it were handled.

Distinct from
[Observability Noise](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-observability-noise): A silent failure emits nothing, while observability noise emits too much to act on.

Distinct from
[Silent Data Corruption](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-silent-data-corruption): A silent failure is any unsurfaced failure, while silent data corruption is invalid data accepted and stored unchecked.

How it is checked

Checked by
[Fail Fast](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-fail-fast), [Logging](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-logging), [Alerting](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-alerting)

## Creational Patterns

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. ## Domain Concerns

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Achievement Tag

- Kind: [artifact](SCHEMA.md#kind-artifact)
- Category: [Domain Concerns](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-domain-concerns)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A formal definition of the tag for a file that defines a recognized milestone and the condition that grants it, filed in an achievements folder.

Example
achievements/first-win.achievement.ts

How it is checked

Checked by
the naming gate, which refuses a filename whose last segment before the extension is an undeclared tag or differs from its folder's tag

Population
Every filename whose concern slot holds the tag, and the folder holding each such file

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file carrying the tag is created, moved or renamed, or the declared vocabulary changes

Refusal
The lint run fails a file whose tag is undeclared or disagrees with its folder

Observation
Each filename parsed by position against the declared concern vocabulary

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, and passes a conforming file

Authoritative side
The declared concern vocabulary, which a filename's tag and its folder conform to

Depends on
Not answered

## Error Handling / Resilience

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### All-Or-Nothing Failure

- Kind: [anti-pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-anti-pattern)
- Category: [Error Handling / Resilience](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-error-handling-resilience)
- Layer: [Correctness Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-correctness-core)

Details

Definition
Failing the entire system when one part fails instead of degrading to reduced but working service.

Referenced by
[Graceful Degradation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-graceful-degradation)

How it is checked

Checked by
[Graceful Degradation](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-graceful-degradation)

Population
The term's definition and every architecture edge that names the term

Freshness
A verdict stands until the definition, the term's kind or an edge that names it changes

Refusal
The resolution gate fails an edge that resolves to no term, and a definition that opens as another kind

Observation
The resolution validator's pass over every edge target and every definition opening

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite plants a term no edge names, a dangling dependency and a second check home, and the bundled terms pass

Authoritative side
The term record, which every edge that names the term cites

Depends on
Not answered

Shape it refuses
Not answered

## Infrastructure Concerns

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Abstraction Tag

- Kind: [artifact](SCHEMA.md#kind-artifact)
- Category: [Infrastructure Concerns](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-infrastructure-concerns)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A formal definition of the tag for a file that defines a general base others specialize, filed in an abstractions folder.

Example
abstractions/shape.abstraction.ts

How it is checked

Checked by
the naming gate, which refuses a filename whose last segment before the extension is an undeclared tag or differs from its folder's tag

Population
Every filename whose concern slot holds the tag, and the folder holding each such file

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file carrying the tag is created, moved or renamed, or the declared vocabulary changes

Refusal
The lint run fails a file whose tag is undeclared or disagrees with its folder

Observation
Each filename parsed by position against the declared concern vocabulary

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, and passes a conforming file

Authoritative side
The declared concern vocabulary, which a filename's tag and its folder conform to

Depends on
Not answered

Shape it refuses
Not answered

## Metadata / Self-Description / Declarative Systems

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Client Generation

- Kind: [capability](SCHEMA.md#kind-capability)
- Category: [Metadata / Self-Description / Declarative Systems](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-metadata-self-description-declarative-systems)
- Layer: [Declarative Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-declarative-core)

Details

Definition
The ability to generate client code automatically from an API's self-description.

Referenced by
[Self-Describing API](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-describing-api)

Distinct from
[HATEOAS-style Navigation](LEXICON.md#lexicon-hateoas-style-navigation): Client generation builds client code from an API's self-description ahead of time, while hypermedia navigation follows the links each response returns.

How it is checked

Checked by
[Self-Describing API](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-self-describing-api)

Population
The term's definition and every architecture edge that names the term

Freshness
A verdict stands until the definition, the term's kind or an edge that names it changes

Refusal
The resolution gate fails an edge that resolves to no term, and a definition that opens as another kind

Observation
The resolution validator's pass over every edge target and every definition opening

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite plants a term no edge names, a dangling dependency and a second check home, and the bundled terms pass

Authoritative side
The term record, which every edge that names the term cites

## Metaprogramming / Language-Oriented Architecture

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

## Observability / Auditability / Traceability

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A verdict stands until the definition, the term's kind or an edge that names it changes

Refusal
The resolution gate fails an edge that resolves to no term, and a definition that opens as another kind

Observation
The resolution validator's pass over every edge target and every definition opening

Evidence

The term record, which every edge that names the term cites

## Operations Concerns

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

## Portability / Infrastructure / Deployment

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

## Processing Concerns

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Aggregator Tag

- Kind: [artifact](SCHEMA.md#kind-artifact)
- Category: [Processing Concerns](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-processing-concerns)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A formal definition of the tag for a file that combines many items into one summary value, filed in an aggregators folder.

Example
aggregators/daily-revenue.aggregator.ts

How it is checked

Checked by
the naming gate, which refuses a filename whose last segment before the extension is an undeclared tag or differs from its folder's tag

Population
Every filename whose concern slot holds the tag, and the folder holding each such file

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file carrying the tag is created, moved or renamed, or the declared vocabulary changes

Refusal
The lint run fails a file whose tag is undeclared or disagrees with its folder

Observation
Each filename parsed by position against the declared concern vocabulary

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, and passes a conforming file

Authoritative side
The declared concern vocabulary, which a filename's tag and its folder conform to

Depends on
Not answered

Shape it refuses
Not answered

Details

Definition
A formal definition of the tag for a file that declares the productions a language is parsed by, filed in a grammars folder.

Example
grammars/sql.grammar.ts

How it is checked

Checked by
the naming gate, which refuses a filename whose last segment before the extension is an undeclared tag or differs from its folder's tag

Population
Every filename whose concern slot holds the tag, and the folder holding each such file

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file carrying the tag is created, moved or renamed, or the declared vocabulary changes

Refusal
The lint run fails a file whose tag is undeclared or disagrees with its folder

Observation
Each filename parsed by position against the declared concern vocabulary

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, and passes a conforming file

Authoritative side
The declared concern vocabulary, which a filename's tag and its folder conform to

## Product Concerns

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

## Quality Attributes

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Architecture Compliance

- Kind: [quality-attribute](SCHEMA.md#kind-quality-attribute)
- Category: [Quality Attributes](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-quality-attributes)
- Layer: [Enforcement Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-enforcement-core)

Details

Definition
The degree to which an implementation conforms to its intended architectural rules, boundaries, and constraints.

Referenced by
[Dependency Graph](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-graph), [Static Analysis](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-static-analysis)

How it is checked

Checked by
[Dependency Graph](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-dependency-graph), [Static Analysis](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-static-analysis)

Population
The term's definition and every architecture edge that names the term

Freshness
A verdict stands until the definition, the term's kind or an edge that names it changes

Refusal
The resolution gate fails an edge that resolves to no term, and a definition that opens as another kind

Observation
The resolution validator's pass over every edge target and every definition opening

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite plants a term no edge names, a dangling dependency and a second check home, and the bundled terms pass

Authoritative side
The term record, which every edge that names the term cites

Depends on
Not answered

Shape it refuses
Not answered

the tension resolution with control-plane, the tension resolution with leader-election, the tension resolution with consensus, [Eventual Consistency](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-eventual-consistency), the tension resolution with fail-safe, the tension resolution with fail-secure, [Horizontal Scaling](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-horizontal-scaling), [Load Balancing](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-load-balancing), [Failover](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-failover), [Replication](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-replication), [Blue-Green Deployment](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-blue-green-deployment), the tension resolution with single-source-of-truth, the tension resolution with consistency

## Refused Tags

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Agent Memory as a Tag

- Kind: [anti-pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-anti-pattern)
- Category: [Refused Tags](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-refused-tags)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
Tagging a file pattern-memory or agent-memory, where the memory tag already covers what an agent remembers between steps.

Before

```text
agent-memories/scout.agent-memory.ts
```

After

```text
memory/scout.memory.ts
```

How it is checked

Checked by
the naming gate, which refuses the word in the concern slot because no declaration admits it

Population
Every filename that would carry the refused word, and the covering tags each refusal names

Freshness
A verdict stands until a covering tag is renamed or removed, or the refused word is admitted by an approved edit

Refusal
The lint run fails a filename carrying the refused word as its concern

Observation
Each refused word resolved through its covering-tag edges, which the resolution gate follows

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite lints a file whose concern slot holds an undeclared word and passes a file carrying a declared tag

Authoritative side
The covering tags, which a refused word resolves to, so admitting the word is an approved edit to the vocabulary

Depends on
[Memory Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-memory-tag)

Shape it refuses
Not answered

## Runtime Concerns

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Activator Tag

- Kind: [artifact](SCHEMA.md#kind-artifact)
- Category: [Runtime Concerns](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-runtime-concerns)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
A formal definition of the tag for a file that switches a prepared component into its active state when its trigger arrives, filed in an activators folder.

Example
activators/voice-command.activator.ts

How it is checked

Checked by
the naming gate, which refuses a filename whose last segment before the extension is an undeclared tag or differs from its folder's tag

Population
Every filename whose concern slot holds the tag, and the folder holding each such file

Freshness
A verdict stands until a file carrying the tag is created, moved or renamed, or the declared vocabulary changes

Refusal
The lint run fails a file whose tag is undeclared or disagrees with its folder

Observation
Each filename parsed by position against the declared concern vocabulary

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, and passes a conforming file

Authoritative side
The declared concern vocabulary, which a filename's tag and its folder conform to

Depends on
Not answered

Shape it refuses
Not answered

## Runtime Discovery / Dynamic Binding

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Capability Addition without Core Modification

- Kind: [capability](SCHEMA.md#kind-capability)
- Category: [Runtime Discovery / Dynamic Binding](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-runtime-discovery-dynamic-binding)
- Layer: [Extensibility Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-extensibility-core)

Details

Definition
The ability to add new capabilities at runtime without modifying the core.

Referenced by
[Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility)

How it is checked

Checked by
[Runtime Extensibility](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-runtime-extensibility)

Population
The term's definition and every architecture edge that names the term

Freshness
A verdict stands until the definition, the term's kind or an edge that names it changes

Refusal
The resolution gate fails an edge that resolves to no term, and a definition that opens as another kind

Observation
The resolution validator's pass over every edge target and every definition opening

Evidence
Watched to fire and to accept: a suite plants a term no edge names, a dangling dependency and a second check home, and the bundled terms pass

Authoritative side
The term record, which every edge that names the term cites

Depends on
Not answered

Shape it refuses
Not answered

## Schema / Canonical Data / Semantics

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

Referenced by

Distinct from
[Claimed Foreign Tree](LEXICON.md#lexicon-claimed-foreign-tree): Duplicated authority is two owners for one fact, while a claimed foreign tree is governing names another runtime owns.

Distinct from
[Depth-Relief Container](LEXICON.md#lexicon-depth-relief-container): Duplicated authority is two owners for one fact, while a depth-relief container is a container declared to shorten a path.

Distinct from
[Magic Value](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-magic-value): Duplicated authority is two owning copies of a fact, while a magic value is a fact written as an unexplained literal, however many times.

Distinct from
[Ignore-List Silencing](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ignore-list-silencing): Duplicated authority is two owners for one fact, while ignore-list silencing removes a file from the taxonomy to hide a finding.

## Security Privacy Compliance

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. ## SOLID / Object-Oriented Design

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

### Contract Preservation

- Kind: [constraint](SCHEMA.md#kind-constraint)
- Category: [SOLID / Object-Oriented Design](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-solid-object-oriented-design)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
The requirement that a subtype honor every behavioral guarantee of the type it replaces.

Referenced by
[Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-liskov-substitution)

Distinct from
[Invariant](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-invariant): Contract preservation binds a subtype to all of its base type's guarantees, while an invariant is one guarantee that holds in every state.

Distinct from
[Postconditions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-postconditions): Contract preservation binds a subtype to every guarantee, while a postcondition is the one an operation gives on return.

Distinct from
[Preconditions](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-preconditions): Contract preservation binds a subtype to every guarantee, while a precondition is what an operation needs before it runs.

How it is checked

Checked by
[Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-liskov-substitution)

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. ## Taxonomy / Classification / Naming

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.

Distinct from

Distinct from
[Ignore Declaration](LEXICON.md#lexicon-ignore-declaration): A compound marker exempts the name and keeps the placement governed, while the ignore declaration removes a name from the taxonomy entirely.

Distinct from
[Structurally Exempt File](LEXICON.md#lexicon-structurally-exempt-file): A compound marker is a word in the filename, while a structurally exempt file is exempt because of how it is resolved.

Distinct from
[Test Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-test-tag): A compound marker is the class of exempting words, while the test marker is one of them.

Distinct from
[Tests](LEXICON.md#lexicon-tests): A compound marker is a filename word, while tests are the executable checks a test file holds.

- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
Reporting an undeclared word without naming the declared word that covers it, so the developer's or the model's next attempt is another guess and the closed set reads as an obstacle rather than a map.

Referenced by
[Guided Vocabulary Refusal](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-guided-vocabulary-refusal)

Distinct from
[Borrowed Synonymy](LEXICON.md#lexicon-borrowed-synonymy): An unguided refusal names no covering word, while borrowed synonymy judges overlap from everyday senses instead of roles.

How it is checked

Checked by

### Vocabulary Inflation

- Kind: [anti-pattern](SCHEMA.md#kind-anti-pattern)
- Category: [Taxonomy / Classification / Naming](LEXICON.md#lexicon-category-taxonomy-classification-naming)
- Layer: [Structural Core](SCHEMA.md#layer-structural-core)

Details

Definition
Admitting a word whose role a declared word already covers, such as a synonym or an abbreviation of it, so one role gets two words and classification gets two right answers.

Aliases
Overlapping Word

Referenced by
[Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary), [Agnostic-First Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-agnostic-first-vocabulary), [Externally Resolved Slot](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-externally-resolved-slot)

Distinct from
[Index as a Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-index-as-a-tag): Vocabulary inflation is the class of admitting an overlapping word, while index as a tag is one refused word of it.

Distinct from
[Adjective Slot Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-adjective-slot-word): Vocabulary inflation admits a word whose role is already covered, while an adjective slot word admits a word that names no role.

Distinct from
[Duplicated Authority](LEXICON.md#lexicon-duplicated-authority): Vocabulary inflation is two words for one role, while duplicated authority is two owners for one fact.

Distinct from
[Instance Identifier Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-instance-identifier-word): Vocabulary inflation adds a second word for a kind, while an instance identifier adds an entry instead of a kind.

Distinct from
[Measurement Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-measurement-word): Vocabulary inflation adds a synonym of a role, while a measurement word adds a quantity.

Distinct from
[Nominalized Process Word](LEXICON.md#lexicon-nominalized-process-word): Vocabulary inflation adds a synonym of a declared role, while a nominalized process word adds an activity.

Distinct from
[Plural Subject](LEXICON.md#lexicon-plural-subject): Vocabulary inflation adds a synonym, while a plural subject uses a real noun in the wrong number.

Distinct from
[Saturated Role Tag](LEXICON.md#lexicon-saturated-role-tag): Vocabulary inflation adds a second word for one role, while a saturated role tag uses one word for every role.

How it is checked

Checked by
[Closed Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-closed-vocabulary), [Agnostic-First Vocabulary](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-agnostic-first-vocabulary), [Externally Resolved Slot](PRINCIPLES.md#architecture-externally-resolved-slot)

## Transactions / State / Concurrency

Every term in this category is listed as one record, with its kind, its definition and its aliases, the principles whose relations name it, the principle or contract that carries the same name where one exists, and the layer its category belongs to. A tag category also gives each term an example, which is the file the tag places or the rename from a refused word onto a covering tag.
